title: Carnatic Sultanate
capsule: The Carnatic Sultanate (Nawabate of Arcot) emerged in 1710 when Saadatullah Khan I transformed a Mughal subah—established in 1692 under Zulfiqar Khan—into a hereditary domain covering much of southeastern India. Its capital shifted from Gingee to Arcot, and later to Chepauk near Madras, as the nawabs balanced Mughal nominal suzerainty, Maratha pressure, and European trading companies. The mid-18th-century wars of succession drew in both the French and British East India Companies, whose rivalry at Arcot (1751) effectively made the Nawabs British clients after Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah (r. 1749–1795). The British East India Company assumed administrative control in 1801, and the line ended definitively in 1855 when the last nawab died without a male heir and Britain applied the doctrine of lapse.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Carnatic Sultanate's boundaries are reasonably attested through Mughal administrative records and British East India Company surveys, though frontier zones contested with Mysore and the Marathas are less precisely defined.
